title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction: The page is the blank back of a typed sheet. The typed text showing through in mirror image is the beginning of the typed page transcribed as 'next page': the Z(S') ≅ G×_S W, principal-bundle and diagram (D) material from an SGA3-style homogeneous-space draft citing Exp. VI and VIII. On this verso Grothendieck wrote a short proof-plan, not connected to that typed text. It reads roughly: 'Ceci prouve [?], avec les indications [suivantes]: (ii) ⇒ (i) ⇔ (iv) ⇒ (iii) ⇒ (v)'. Each arrow carries a justification. Under (ii)⇒(i): something like 'par continuité / spécialisation des familles linéaires et jacobiennes'. Under (i)⇔(iv): 'définition de la K-équivalence des cycles'. Under (iv)⇒(iii): 'R.R.' (Riemann–Roch). The arrow (iii)⇒(v) has no justification. Given the folder's subject (algebraic cycles; standard, Hodge and Tate conjectures), the list (i)–(v) is almost certainly a chain of equivalence relations on algebraic cycles, or of statements about them. Read that way: (ii)⇒(i) passes from a linear/rational-type equivalence to an algebraic-type one, by specialising linear systems and Jacobian (Picard/Albanese) families. (i)⇔(iv) identifies a cycle-theoretic equivalence with its K-theoretic counterpart (equivalence of classes in K_0 or a filtered K_0), true by definition. (iv)⇒(iii) uses Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch: the Chern character identifies K_0⊗Q with Chow⊗Q, transporting K-equivalence to a cycle-level equivalence such as homological/numerical up to torsion. (iii)⇒(v) is presumably the weakest implication, e.g. homological ⇒ numerical. The page is an outline of a comparison of adequate equivalence relations via K-theory and Riemann–Roch, as in SGA 6 and the standard-conjectures circle of ideas.
errors: No mathematical error can be checked: the statements (i)–(v) are not on this page and the sketch is only a list of justifications. The exact identity of (i)–(v) is conjectural from context.

ideas.what: Chain of implications between equivalence relations on algebraic cycles, with one step justified by definition of K-equivalence and one by Riemann–Roch
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of adequate equivalence relations via K_0 and the Chern character (GRR); K-theoretic vs cycle-theoretic equivalences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Riemann–Roch 1957, SGA 6 1966–67); Manin 1968; Kleiman 1968/1994 on equivalence relations
ideas.where_published: SGA 6 (K-theory, γ-filtration, Riemann–Roch); Borel–Serre exposition of GRR; 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) for the equivalence-relation context

ideas.what: Specialisation of linear and Jacobian families to pass between linear/rational and algebraic-type equivalence
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic equivalence via Picard/Albanese varieties; specialisation of cycles

deep.surprise_reason: This is a terse proof-plan scribbled on reused scratch paper. The ideas it points to (K-equivalence of cycles, Riemann–Roch comparison with cycle equivalences, specialisation of Jacobian families) are standard and published by Grothendieck and his school. It is too fragmentary to contain anything new.
